# Judith Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_012_page_001.jpg

---

**1** He gave orders for her to be brought to the room where his silver vessels were laid out, and he commanded that she be served from his own food and poured from his own wine.

**2** But Judith refused. "I cannot eat any of this," she said. "It would be a violation. I have my own provisions — they will be enough."

**3** Holofernes frowned. "But what happens when what you brought runs out? We have no one here from your people to resupply you."

**4** "As you live, my lord," Judith replied, "your servant will not run out of what she has until the LORD has finished doing through my hand what he has planned."

**5** His servants led her to her tent, and she slept until the middle of the night. She rose before the morning watch and sent word to Holofernes:

**6** "Let my lord command that your servant be allowed to go out for prayer."

**7** Holofernes told his guards not to stop her. She stayed in the camp three days. Each night she went out to the valley of Bethulia, bathed herself at the spring near the camp,

**8** and when she came back up from the water, she prayed to the LORD God of Israel to show her the path — to lift up the sons of his people.

**9** She returned clean and stayed in her tent until she ate her food in the evening.

**10** On the fourth day, Holofernes threw a private banquet for his personal attendants — just them, no officers invited.

**11** He called Bagoas, the eunuch who managed all his personal affairs. "Go," he said, "and talk that Hebrew woman into coming to us. Tell her to eat and drink with us.

**12** It would be an embarrassment if we let a woman like that go without sleeping with her. If we can't win her over, she'll be laughing at us."

**13** Bagoas left and went to Judith. "Don't let this beautiful young woman be too shy to come honor my lord with her presence," he said with a smile. "Come drink wine with us and enjoy yourself. Today, be like the daughters of the Assyrians who serve in Nebuchadnezzar's own house."

**14** Judith looked at him. "Who am I to refuse my lord? Whatever pleases him, I will do at once. And this will be my joy until the day I die."

**15** She got up and put on her full array — her clothes, her jewelry, every piece of her feminine adornment. Her servant went on ahead and spread out on the floor before Holofernes the fleeces she had been given by Bagoas for her daily use, so she could recline on them to eat.

**16** Judith came in and lay down. And Holofernes' heart was seized — completely undone at the sight of her. His desire was overwhelming. He burned to sleep with her. He had been watching her, scheming for just this opportunity, since the moment he first laid eyes on her.

**17** "Drink now," said Holofernes. "Be glad with us."

**18** "I will drink gladly, my lord," said Judith. "Today my life has been lifted higher than all the days since I was born."

**19** She took what her servant had prepared and ate and drank in front of him.

**20** And Holofernes was delighted. He drank more wine that night than he had drunk on any single day of his entire life.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The chapter turns entirely on physical and psychological suspense. Judith's three-night prayer routine and her food discipline are not mere piety — they are her cover. She has constructed an alibi and a routine. Holofernes' drunkenness in v. 20 is the mechanism of the coming execution. The chapter ends at the exact moment of maximum danger and maximum opportunity. Judith's toast in v. 18 is the darkest irony in the book.*
